properties.entry: Dropdown

Dropdown and MultiDropdown from ui-components are drop-downs that look the same in every browser and take the colors of the theme. Everything happens in the browser: the list opens, filters and is navigated with the keyboard without a request to the server. The native select stays in the page, hidden, and holds the choice, so a form posts it as always and an Ajax behavior on its change event is notified as with a native select.

Use the arrow keys to move through the options, Enter or Space to choose and Escape to close; type into the filter, which a list gets from eight options on, or always when asked to. A multiple drop-down stays open while options are toggled and shows the chosen ones as chips in the theme's colors, each with an x removing it; Backspace on the button removes the last one. The text below the form follows every choice via Ajax.

The countries chosen most come first, in a group of their own, and the others under them. The button below the form opens a modal dialog choosing a unit of measure from a long list of long options in groups, the few used most first and the others by what they measure: the open list reaches over the footer of the dialog rather than being cut by its body, a long option wraps onto more lines, and the filter hides a group none of whose options match.

Piece (pc): one item counted as a whole, such as a chair, a licence or a set sold as one
Kilogram (kg): the base unit of mass of the International System of Units, 1,000 grams
Metre (m): the base unit of length of the International System of Units, 100 centimetres
Litre (l): the volume of one cubic decimetre, for liquids and for goods sold in bulk
Hour (h): 60 minutes, for the work and the services billed by the time spent on them
Pair (pr): two items sold together, such as shoes, gloves or the two halves of a set
Dozen (dz): twelve items sold together, such as eggs or the bottles of a case
Box (bx): the items of one box or carton, as many as the supplier packs into it
Pallet (plt): the goods of one pallet, as many as the supplier stacks on it for shipping
Milligram (mg): a thousandth of a gram, for medicines, vitamins and other small doses
Gram (g): a thousandth of a kilogram, for food, spices and other light goods
Tonne (t): 1,000 kilograms, for building materials, grain and other heavy goods
Ounce (oz): an imperial and US unit of mass of about 28.35 grams, for food and precious metals
Pound (lb): an imperial and US unit of mass of 16 ounces, about 453.6 grams
Millimetre (mm): a thousandth of a metre, for the sizes of parts and the thickness of sheets
Centimetre (cm): a hundredth of a metre, for fabrics, furniture and garments
Kilometre (km): 1,000 metres, for the distances travelled and the cables laid
Inch (in): an imperial and US unit of length of exactly 2.54 centimetres, for screens and pipes
Foot (ft): an imperial and US unit of length of 12 inches, exactly 30.48 centimetres
Yard (yd): an imperial and US unit of length of 3 feet, exactly 91.44 centimetres
Mile (mi): an imperial and US unit of length of 1,760 yards, about 1.609 kilometres
Square metre (m²): the area of a square of one metre a side, for floors, walls and land
Hectare (ha): 10,000 square metres, the area of a square of 100 metres a side, for fields
Square foot (ft²): the area of a square of one foot a side, about 0.093 square metres
Acre (ac): an imperial and US unit of area of 43,560 square feet, about 4,047 square metres
Millilitre (ml): a thousandth of a litre, for medicines, cosmetics and samples
Centilitre (cl): a hundredth of a litre, for the drinks of a bar and small bottles
Cubic metre (m³): 1,000 litres, for water, gas, concrete, timber and earth
US gallon (gal): a US unit of volume of 128 fluid ounces, about 3.785 litres, for fuels
Second (s): the base unit of time of the International System of Units
Minute (min): 60 seconds, for calls, parking and the other services billed by the minute
Day (d): 24 hours, for rentals, stays and the work billed by the day
Week (wk): seven days, for the rentals and subscriptions billed by the week
Month (mo): a calendar month, for rents, subscriptions and maintenance contracts
Watt-hour (Wh): the energy of one watt for an hour, for batteries and small devices
Kilowatt-hour (kWh): 1,000 watt-hours, for the electricity a home or a business uses
Megajoule (MJ): a million joules, 3.6 of them being one kilowatt-hour, for heat and fuels
